tasks.title: Compute daily review-count history and retention-rate metrics
acceptance_criteria: Given a range of past review-log entries, returns per-day counts of reviews performed, including days with zero reviews
Retention rate = (# graded Good or Easy) / (# graded total) over the selected window, exposed as a percentage
Functions are pure and independently unit-testable without a UI

tasks.title: Exclude demo-seeded decks/cards from aggregate stats and streak calculations
acceptance_criteria: Decks/cards flagged as demo-seeded are filtered out before any aggregate/overall stats computation by default
Streak calculation ignores review activity tied to demo-seeded cards
A user-created deck named similarly to demo content is still included (filter is by seed flag, not name/heuristic)

tasks.title: Daily review-count history chart screen
acceptance_criteria: Renders a chart/list of review counts per day sourced from T-016 output
Respects demo-seed exclusion from T-017 by default
Screen has a loading state distinct from its empty state

tasks.title: Retention rate stats screen
acceptance_criteria: Displays retention rate (% Good/Easy) sourced from T-016 output
Respects demo-seed exclusion from T-017 by default
Value updates when the stats window/filter changes

tasks.title: Designed empty/sparse-data states for all stats screens
acceptance_criteria: Zero-data case (no reviews ever) shows a designed empty state, not a blank chart or crash
Sparse-data case (e.g. 1-2 data points) renders without div-by-zero or misleading 100%/0% placeholders
No stats screen throws or shows a raw error when the underlying dataset is empty

tasks.title: CSV export generator (front, back, note)
acceptance_criteria: Produces a CSV with header front,back,note
Note column is emitted empty (not omitted) when a card has no note
Fields containing commas, quotes, or newlines are properly quoted/escaped per RFC 4180

tasks.title: CSV import parser with malformed-row error taxonomy
acceptance_criteria: Accepts front (required), back (required), note (optional) columns
Handles CRLF and LF line endings and strips a UTF-8 BOM if present without corrupting the first field

Produces a distinct, named error reason per malformed row: empty front, empty back, wrong column count, embedded-comma/quote parse failure, bad encoding/BOM — no row is ever silently dropped, each maps to exactly one reason code

tasks.title: Duplicate detection for CSV import
acceptance_criteria: Flags rows as duplicates on case-sensitive exact front+back match against other rows within the same import file
Flags rows as duplicates against existing non-archived cards in the target deck (archived cards are not considered)
Duplicate is reported as its own distinct reason, separate from the malformed-row reasons in T-022

tasks.title: CSV import screen with preview-before-commit step
acceptance_criteria: User selects a CSV file, sees a preview listing every row's outcome (import / error reason / duplicate reason) before anything is written
No card is created in the target deck until the user explicitly confirms the preview
Confirming only commits rows that passed validation and were not flagged as duplicates (or duplicates the user explicitly chose to include, if that affordance exists)

tasks.title: CSV export screen/entry point
acceptance_criteria: User can trigger export of a deck's cards to a CSV file via T-021's generator
Exported file is accessible/shareable through the platform's standard file-save or share flow

tasks.title: Lossless export/re-import round-trip test suite
acceptance_criteria: Exporting a deck then re-importing the resulting CSV reproduces identical front/back/note content for every card
Cards with no note round-trip without introducing a spurious note value
Cards containing commas, quotes, and newlines in their fields round-trip byte-for-byte on the text content

tasks.title: CSV import fixtures: real-world export plus hand-crafted edge cases
acceptance_criteria: Test fixtures include at least one CSV actually produced by exporting from this app (or another real tool) unmodified by hand, exercising realistic quoting/encoding
Additional hand-crafted fixtures cover each malformed-row reason from T-022 and the duplicate case from T-023 individually
Test suite asserts the exact error/duplicate reason produced for each fixture row, not just pass/fail

tasks.title: Due-count computation recomputed at refresh points
acceptance_criteria: Exposes a function computing the current due-card count from live data, with no cached/stale value returned
Called at app foreground, app background transition, immediately after a review session ends, and on day rollover
Two calls made on either side of a day-rollover boundary (with no other data change) can yield different counts, proving it's not fixed at a single computed-once value

tasks.title: Local daily reminder notification scheduling service
acceptance_criteria: User can pick one time of day; exactly one local notification is scheduled for that time, replacing any prior schedule (not stacking)
Scheduling re-reads the current due count from T-028 at fire time rather than baking in a count computed when the user set the time
Turning the feature off cancels the pending scheduled notification

tasks.title: Notification body contains only numeric due-count
acceptance_criteria: Notification body text is limited to a number (e.g. '12 cards due') with no card content, deck name, or subject-matter text interpolated in
Code review/test asserts no deck title, card front/back, or tag text ever reaches the notification payload

tasks.title: Suppress notification when due count is zero
acceptance_criteria: At scheduled fire time, if the freshly recomputed due count is 0, no notification is shown
If due count later becomes 0 before the scheduled time (e.g. user already reviewed everything), the pending notification is cancelled rather than firing with '0 cards due'

tasks.title: Notification settings UI: time picker and permission request
acceptance_criteria: Settings screen lets the user enable/disable the daily reminder and pick its time
Enabling for the first time triggers the OS permission prompt via the platform notification API

tasks.title: Graceful handling of notification permission denial
acceptance_criteria: If the user denies the OS permission prompt, the app does not crash and the toggle reflects the denied state instead of appearing silently enabled
Screen shows a clear message and a path to opt in later (e.g. a button that deep-links to OS notification settings)
Re-checking permission status on screen focus updates the UI if the user grants permission from OS settings afterward
